source: William Lilly Christian Astrology first edition 1647, Wellcome b30338724
original_heading: Judgements upon the fourth House. Concerning Parents and Patrimony of the Father
limitations: These are historical claims about parents, father status, ancestry, survival, not actual diagnoses or individual forecasts.
Day/night solar/Saturn alternatives must not collapse to a single branch.
Parental original chart claimed preferable, compared to child chart.
Passage includes glyphs of questionable identification; preserve as unresolved.
No full diplomatic transcription or independent human outcome validation.

groups.subject: Unnumbered fourth-house heading and source scope

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Judgements upon the fourth House
claims.historical_only_meaning: A new unnumbered substantive natal source section starts at original first-edition PDF603, separate from sibling number.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Concerning Parents ... Patrimony of the Father
claims.historical_only_meaning: The main original unnumbered source concerns father and patrimony/parental status; later mother chapter has its own separate heading.

groups.subject: Four father significator categories, sect differentiation

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: first, the fourth house
claims.historical_only_meaning: The fourth house itself is first in Lilly's hierarchy for the father and his circumstances.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: secondly, the Lord thereof
claims.historical_only_meaning: The fourth-house ruler is an additional and distinct father significator.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Sun in a diurnall Geniture
claims.historical_only_meaning: In daytime nativities the Sun is assigned father significator status; the birth sect must be known.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Saturn in a nocturnall
claims.historical_only_meaning: In nighttime nativities Saturn substitutes for Sun under this father-source selection; no unconditional same-luminary method.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Planet or Planets in the fourth
claims.historical_only_meaning: Any planet(s) occupying the fourth house form a fourth category of father indicators.

groups.subject: Strong/benefic aspects, negative and mixed parental-fortune conditions

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: these Significators or the most of them strong and fortunate
claims.historical_only_meaning: A favorable father assessment requires all or the majority of listed significators to be strong and fortunate.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: good aspect of Jupiter or Venus
claims.historical_only_meaning: Supportive aspect to Jupiter or Venus is another separate prerequisite or supporting testimony, not sufficient alone.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: happy condition of the Father after the Childs birth
claims.historical_only_meaning: The source claims favorable paternal condition after the child's birth, without actual family evidence.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Significators be unfortunate and impedited
claims.historical_only_meaning: Unfortunate and impeded significators are Lilly's explicit opposite branch.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: dejected and low condition ... many misfortunes
claims.historical_only_meaning: Under adverse testimony the source alleges low paternal status and misfortunes, not independently verified outcomes.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: some be strong and others weak
claims.historical_only_meaning: The mixed father indicators are not forced into either positive or negative extreme.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: they tend to a mediocrity
claims.historical_only_meaning: For mixed cases the author assigns a moderate result rather than certainty of prosperity or poverty.

groups.subject: Fourth-house inhabitants and strongest-planet priority; father chart precedence

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: according to the nature of the Planet or Planets occupying fourth
claims.historical_only_meaning: In mixed configurations the original bases the parent's fortunes on planetary inhabitants of the fourth house.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: if there be many therein
claims.historical_only_meaning: More than one planet in the fourth is expressly contemplated as a selection ambiguity.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: he that is most dignified preferred in judgment
claims.historical_only_meaning: Among multiple occupants the most dignified should be preferred rather than averaging all descriptions.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: best drawn from the Fathers own Nativity
claims.historical_only_meaning: Lilly states that evaluating the father from his OWN natal chart is preferable to the child's chart; different input requirements matter.

groups.subject: Fortunate fourth-house planets and angular/succedent dignity

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: fortunate Planets in fourth
claims.historical_only_meaning: Fortunate planets occupying fourth are a specified positive parental-fortune indicator.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: their Lords in angles or succedants
claims.historical_only_meaning: The rulers of those fortunate occupants must occupy angular or succedent houses for the favorable pattern.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: well disposed ... no aspect to the Infortunes
claims.historical_only_meaning: Favorable placement and absence of harsh malefic aspect are additional qualifications.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: condition of the Parents laudable and good
claims.historical_only_meaning: The author asserts favorable parental standing under the compound condition, not a measured life outcome.

groups.subject: Adverse cadent/afflicted parent indicators and graded outcome

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Significators in cadent houses
claims.historical_only_meaning: Cadency of relevant parental significators is one of the asserted negative conditions.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: unfortunate starrs in the fourth
claims.historical_only_meaning: Unfortunate planets physically in fourth are listed as an additional adverse alternative.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Lords of the places ... afflicted of the Infortunes
claims.historical_only_meaning: Affliction of applicable house rulers by malefics forms a further alternative negative trigger.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Parents subject to many misfortunes
claims.historical_only_meaning: The source forecasts general parental difficulties on those sources, without calibrated probability.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: greatnesse ... by strength or debility of the Significators
claims.historical_only_meaning: Magnitude of the alleged good or bad fate should be graded by significator strength, with no numeric score given.

groups.subject: Fourth ruler reception or good aspect to ascendant ruler

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Lord of the fourth in Reception with Lord of ascendant
claims.historical_only_meaning: Mutual reception of fourth ruler with the first ruler is one historical positive parent condition.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: or in Trine with him
claims.historical_only_meaning: Trine between the fourth and ascendant rulers is a separate positive alternative to reception.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: or Sextile with him
claims.historical_only_meaning: Sextile is another distinct positive alternative, not a required simultaneous trine.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: flourishing condition in the Father
claims.historical_only_meaning: Lilly claims these configurations indicate paternal flourishing, not a verified actual father life record.

groups.subject: Sun or Jupiter in fourth; father ruler own dignity and esteemed status

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Sun or Jupiter in fourth
claims.historical_only_meaning: A Sun or Jupiter occupant in fourth is said to indicate an esteemed father, using distinct alternatives.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Father to be a man of good quality
claims.historical_only_meaning: The author associates the fourth-house Sun/Jupiter condition with paternal standing rather than longevity.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Planet signifies Father be in angle or succedant
claims.historical_only_meaning: The father significator should occupy an angular or succedent house as part of the high-status branch.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: in his owne house or Exaltation
claims.historical_only_meaning: The same significator must additionally have domicile or exaltation dignity; otherwise result is not unconditional.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Father to be a man of esteeme and quality
claims.historical_only_meaning: The compound father-status condition alleges public esteem without human observations.

groups.subject: Mixed fourth-house conjunction and contrasting father longevity clauses

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Sun Saturn Mars and Mercury in the fourth
claims.historical_only_meaning: Lilly prints a clustered list of planetary glyphs in fourth and states a short life; the scope of AND/OR is uncertain.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Father will live but a while
claims.historical_only_meaning: The author asserts a short paternal lifespan for that cluster, without a real-person survival timeline.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Jupiter and Venus by any application or aspect
claims.historical_only_meaning: Jupiter/Venus are named as additional source planets in a favorable father-longevity branch.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: in configuration with Sun or Saturn
claims.historical_only_meaning: The benefics' relations to Sun/Saturn as relevant father significators are included, under sect considerations.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: friendly aspect between them ... both strong
claims.historical_only_meaning: The planets must have a friendly aspect and both be strong in the favorable longevity branch.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: promise long life to the Father
claims.historical_only_meaning: Lilly claims paternal longevity under the combined testimony; no historical cases are verified.

groups.subject: Lunar-node/luminary combinations and parental descent contrast

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Sun with North Node ... Moon in fourth
claims.historical_only_meaning: The source associates a particular Sun/node configuration and Moon in fourth with parental status; source glyph must be independently read.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Father to be of good Parents
claims.historical_only_meaning: One asserted result of the preceding combination is good paternal ancestry/standing.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Native not long lived
claims.historical_only_meaning: The same cluster assigns short life to the chart native, not the father; keep distinct persons and no validity claim.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Sun better dignified then Moon
claims.historical_only_meaning: The relative dignity of Sun and Moon is used to compare father/mother descent rather than predict absolute wealth.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Father better descended then the Mother
claims.historical_only_meaning: Lilly claims father from higher-status origins when Sun outranks Moon, not an observed social-class inference.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: and so the contrary
claims.historical_only_meaning: The opposite relative dignity is alleged to reverse the parental descent verdict; operator/tie rules unspecified.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Sun and Moon in [Mars glyph] masculine Signe
claims.historical_only_meaning: The exact original glyph and grammar in the masculine-sign parental outcome clause are uncertain; do not encode.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: shew dignity of the Father
claims.historical_only_meaning: The author attributes paternal dignity to the masculine-sign/luminary condition.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: short life to the Mother ... before the Father
claims.historical_only_meaning: The clause simultaneously makes a maternal earlier-death prediction; this remains source history, not medical evidence.

groups.subject: Peregrine twelfth-house father indicator and unfavorable Sun combinations

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Sun or Lord of fourth peregrine in twelfth
claims.historical_only_meaning: Either Sun or fourth ruler peregrine in twelfth is alleged to predict low paternal condition.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Father of a very low condition
claims.historical_only_meaning: The preceding 12th-house configuration is linked to low paternal standing, an unsupported period social category.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Sun conjunct South Node and cadent
claims.historical_only_meaning: An adverse Sun/node combination with cadency is alleged to indicate poor parental standing; exact sign operator needs specialist check.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: in a Bestiall Signe
claims.historical_only_meaning: An additional sign-class requirement is specified in the adverse parental status branch.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: shewes abject Parents
claims.historical_only_meaning: The source asserts low parental social standing under the planetary combination, without human study.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Sun and Saturn in cadent houses and [Mars glyph]
claims.historical_only_meaning: Lilly adds an adverse Sun/Saturn configuration, with a glyph between conditions still uncertain.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: short life to the Father
claims.historical_only_meaning: The author alleges paternal short lifespan from Sun/Saturn conditions; no medical validation and no timeline.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Saturn infortuning Sun
claims.historical_only_meaning: An afflicting Saturn–Sun relationship forms an additional claimed death-cause source.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Father dyes of Melancholly
claims.historical_only_meaning: Lilly attributes paternal death to melancholy; this is not a medical diagnosis or causal evidence.

groups.subject: Separate printed mother chapter boundary navigation only

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CXXII Of the Mother
claims.historical_only_meaning: The next printed numbered chapter starts after horizontal divider on PDF604 and is substantive mother source to extract separately.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Mothers Significators ... tenth house
claims.historical_only_meaning: Only the opening of CXXII's indicator list is witnessed, not admitted as a fourth-house father condition.
